summary: ARES (Martian Tactical HUD) is an integrated Mars exploration platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It combines a 3D interactive Martian globe, NASA-related datasets, environmental telemetry, rover imagery, and hazard detection to help astronauts and mission planners explore Mars safely. The system provides real-time weather information, terrain visualization, geodesic route planning, automated hazard avoidance, and proximity alerts. Built using a Flask backend and WebGL frontend, ARES aims to make Martian surface exploration more accessible, efficient, and reliable, even when external data sources are unavailable.
details:
Project Details

ARES, the Martian Tactical HUD is a platform that helps people explore the Martian surface more safely and efficiently. ARES gives an interactive screen that shows Martian terrain, weather data, pictures from rovers, science data and automatic route planning.

How It Works:

ARES relies on a Flask-based Python server to gather, clean and arrange data from Kaggle, NASA missions and rover observations. The server cleans the data does math, changes temperatures and groups data by time. If external data is missing ARES uses fallback methods. Automatically creates terrain maps to keep working.

The front end shows a 3D globe built with WebGL, Three.js and globe.gl letting users see craters, science zones, dangerous areas and weather data. Users can click any spot on the globe to view rover pictures and surface details.

ARES also plans routes that follow the planet’s curves and checks each path for danger. If a route crosses a hazard ARES finds a detour. ARES sends alerts when a chosen point or explorer gets near ground.

Key Benefits and Intended Impact:

- ARES gives one place to find and look at types of Martian data.

- ARES makes it easier to see the situation by showing 3D terrain that you can interact with.

- ARES helps explorers stay safe by spotting danger and automatically changing routes.

- ARES supplies weather details such as temperature, pressure and wind speed.

- ARES lets you inspect the surface by showing images taken by rovers.

- ARES stays reliable by storing data locally and using backups when outside data fails.

ARES aims to help Martian missions. Mission planners, scientists and astronauts can use ARES to learn about surface conditions, spot hazards and map paths.

Technologies and Tools Used:

Programming Languages: Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS.

Backend: Flask and REST API architecture.

Frontend: Three.js, globe.gl, WebGL and Turf.js.

Data Processing: Pandas and NumPy.

Dataset Integration: Kaggle and kagglehub.

Data Sources: NASA data, MEDA weather data, Mars crater lists and rover photo collections.

Deployment: Render cloud hosting.

Creativity and Innovation:

ARES is creative because it mixes Martian exploration tools into one interactive interface. Than showing terrain, weather, science and danger on separate screens ARES puts them all together in one 3D world.

ARES builds terrain automatically with Brownian motion noise and crater shapes to make the surface look realistic.

By adding route planning detours, rover pictures and alerts ARES becomes more than a visual tool; it becomes a real help for exploring safely.

Factors Considered During Development:

During ARES development we paid attention to data access, reliability, speed of visuals, route accuracy and how easy it is to use. We worked hard to handle missing data keep downloads with caching keep the system running when outside data fails and speed up 3D rendering.

ARES is built to grow. Future upgrades could add real elevation data from MOLA AI to classify terrain maps of ice, from SWIM and analysis that weighs how safe a spot is.
